note: FH.17 inferred HTTP wrapper precision, with no overlay. `makeRequest({ path })` builds a local options object (`{ url: '/api' + path, method: 'GET' }`) and fetch reads `opts.url`: the inference follows the object, so `makeRequest({ path: '/items' })` mints `endpoint:GET:/api/items`, which pairs the Go route. `Cache.lookup` / `Cache.drop` call `.get(key)` / `.delete(key)` on an untyped field the parser keeps as `<unresolved>` (CH.3c fails open on an unknown type): no HTTP client receiver, so neither seeds a wrapper and `cached()`'s `c.lookup('/items')` / `c.drop('/items')` mint nothing (pre-FH.17 they minted endpoint:GET:/items, paired to GET /api/items by route prefix, and endpoint:DELETE:/items). The typed `new Map()` field's `.get(id)` is dropped by the parser already. `PerformRequest(r, method, path)` in server/api_test.go is a test helper over `http.NewRequest` driving the app's own router: its site `PerformRequest(r, "GET", "/api/stats")` mints `endpoint:GET:/api/stats` with ORIGIN `test_fixture` and pairs nothing, though main.go serves GET /api/stats. The spec's sketch used `httptest.NewRequest`, which no client needle reads; photoprism's helper (the case FH.17 measures) calls `http.NewRequest`, used here. The spec's forbid on `endpoint:GET:<unresolved>` is not kept: the parser itself mints that node for `fetch(opts.url, opts)` and for `this.entries.get(key)`, which a wrapper inference cannot remove; the phantom wrappers' minted endpoints are forbidden instead. Baseline: see the FH.17 commit. Deliberately not bound to a matrix cell: typescript/http_client is already scored.
